title: Article 353 — Effect of Proclamation of Emergency

content.overview: Article 353 provides that while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to any State as to the manner in which the executive power of the State is to be exercised, and the power of Parliament to make laws includes power for the whole or any part of India with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the State List. Laws so made cease to have effect to the extent of incompetence six months after the Proclamation ends, except as to things done or omitted before expiry.
content.glance: During National Emergency: Union may direct States on executive exercise; Parliament may legislate on State List matters. Such laws lapse (prospectively) 6 months after Emergency ends.
content.study:
Article 353 effects of National Emergency:
1. Union executive power extends to giving directions to States as to the manner of exercise of State executive power.
2. Parliament may make laws on State List matters for the whole or any part of India.
3. Post-Emergency: such parliamentary laws cease to have effect (except as to things already done/omitted) six months after the Proclamation has ceased to operate, insofar as they would not have been competent without the Emergency.

Examination: directions to States; State List legislation; 6-month sunset after Emergency.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
1. Union may give directions to States on exercise of State executive power.
2. Parliament may legislate on State List matters.
3. Such laws cease (prospectively) 6 months after Emergency ends, except as to things done or omitted before expiry.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the effect of a Proclamation of Emergency under Article 353?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 353, while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, the executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to any State as to the manner in which the State’s executive power is to be exercised, and Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of India with respect to any matter in the State List. Laws so made that would not have been within Parliament’s competence without the Emergency cease to have effect six months after the Proclamation ends, except as to things done or omitted before such expiry.

examTips: Union directions to States; Parliament on State List; 6-month post-Emergency sunset.

keyTakeaways: Art 353: effects of National Emergency on Union–State powers.
